variants.cost: Per iteration: two exact F evaluations and two exact C projections, separately charged, plus O(d) vector arithmetic. For K iterations the direct implementation uses 2K evaluations and 2K projections. For C=Q×S, each product projection consists of one Q projection and one S projection. No computational cost for implementing these primitives is assumed away.
variants.implementation_details_ref: Source Eq.(6) on printed p.38 gives the mechanism; tuning and performance use the separately stated local joint-L theorem in this batch.
variants.name: Joint-L safe-condition adapter
variants.output: Feasible main last iterate x_K, or the main sequence for asymptotic convergence. Trial points y_k are feasible auxiliary iterates and also converge under the linked conditions.
public_inputs: Nonempty closed convex C subset R^d and exact projection access
Exact F:C->R^d and a verified joint bound L_T>0
Feasible x_0 and fixed eta in (0,1/L_T); an external finite iteration budget K if a finite run is desired
variants.query_and_update: Evaluate F(x_k); set y_k=P_C(x_k-eta F(x_k)); evaluate F(y_k); set x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-eta F(y_k)). The second projection uses the old x_k as its base.
variants.requirements: Finite-dimensional Euclidean geometry, single-valued monotone jointly L_T-Lipschitz F on C, nonempty VI solution set, exact F evaluation and exact Euclidean P_C.
variants.state_and_initialization: Initialize x_0 in C. Retain x_k as the base point for both projections. No knowledge of a solution is required to execute the update; solution existence is a performance assumption.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Choose one fixed eta with 0<eta<1/L_T. For a finite run stop after an externally supplied K>=0 iterations; return x_K. The linked theorem supplies asymptotic convergence and a residual summability bound, not a finite epsilon stopping certificate.
